patients.summary: Retired school librarian who joined in 2016 with hypertension, lipids and a treated 2014 left breast cancer on letrozole. Primary hyperparathyroidism and pseudogout in 2019, bone metastases in 2020, thiazide gout, giant cell arteritis, two hypercalcemia crises in 2024, then chemotherapy, palliative care and a passive wish to die followed by the practice into 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
62-year-old retired high school librarian transferring care. Organized historian; brought a typed list and her bottles.

PROBLEMS SHE BRINGS
- Hypertension for close to ten years, on lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25. Home readings in the 120s-130s.
- High cholesterol, atorvastatin 20 since about 2009, no muscle complaints.
- Left breast cancer found in early 2014: left modified radical mastectomy with sentinel node biopsy, then adjuvant chemo (she does not recall the drug names), then letrozole 2.5 daily, which she still takes. Followed by an outside oncology group once a year. No new lumps, no bone pain.
- Knee arthritis, both sides, aching on stairs; acetaminophen 650 as needed works well enough. Hands stiff in the mornings in winter.
- Osteoporosis on a DXA at her old office a few years back. Never took a medication for it; she is fuzzy on why.
- One calcium oxalate kidney stone around 2010, passed on its own, none since.

SURGERIES: hysterectomy with both ovaries out at 50 (2003); laparoscopic gallbladder removal at 45 (1998); the mastectomy above.

ALLERGIES: penicillin - throat closed as a young woman, treated in an ER. IV contrast - hives after a CT years ago.

FAMILY: mother had invasive breast cancer at 62 and has died. Father had high blood pressure, longstanding gout and kept forming kidney stones. Sister has severe osteoporosis with compression fractures of the spine.

SOCIAL: lives alone, never married. Quit cigarettes around 1996 after roughly 10 pack-years. A glass or two of wine a week. Volunteers at the town library book sale.

ROS otherwise negative.

EXAM: well, slender. Vitals as charted. Mastectomy scar healed, chest wall smooth. Right breast without mass, right axilla clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed port sites. Knees with mild crepitus, no effusion. No edema. Neuro grossly normal.

ASSESSMENT / PLAN
1. Hypertension - at goal on current pair. Continue. CMP today.
2. Hyperlipidemia - continue atorvastatin 20, lipid panel.
3. Breast cancer history - on letrozole through her oncologist. Right diagnostic mammogram this summer; will get her oncology letters.
4. OA knees - acetaminophen, stay active.
5. Osteoporosis - will review the old DXA when records come; revisit treatment then.
6. Remote stone - fluids.
7. Health maintenance: Tdap today. One-time hepatitis C and HIV screening with her blood work. Colonoscopy reportedly 2015, awaiting records.
Release for prior records signed. Return in about 6 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Svetlana, your blood work from Tuesday looks fine. Kidney function, potassium and sugar are normal; cholesterol is where it should be on the atorvastatin. Calcium is at the top of normal, nothing to act on. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. No changes.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
41 pages received by fax from the patient's former internal medicine office. Summary prepared for the PCP:
- Colonoscopy June 2015, normal, no polyps; next due in 10 years.
- Right breast mammogram 2015: benign.
- DXA report (date partly cut off on fax, appears 2013): osteoporosis range at the spine. No treatment note attached.
- Problem list: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, breast cancer s/p left mastectomy, osteoarthritis, nephrolithiasis history.
- Medication list matches what she brought.
Filed under Outside Records. Flagged for PCP review.

documents.title: Outside records reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Old chart reviewed. Colonoscopy 2015 normal, repeat 2025. Mammogram normal. DXA confirms osteoporosis; nothing documented about why no treatment was started. Will raise at a future visit.

documents.title: Oncology survivorship visit
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ONCOLOGY GROUP - SURVIVORSHIP CLINIC
Visit of 05/31/2016. Copy to new primary care physician.

Ms. Foley is now two years out from left modified radical mastectomy with sentinel node biopsy for hormone receptor-positive invasive ductal carcinoma, followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and letrozole. She is tolerating letrozole with mild joint aching. No new breast, chest wall or bone symptoms.

Exam: left chest wall flat, well healed, no nodularity. Right breast and both axillae negative. No supraclavicular nodes.

Plan: continue letrozole 2.5 mg daily. Annual right breast imaging through primary care is fine with us. Return in one year.

Allergies on file: penicillin (anaphylaxis), iodinated contrast (urticaria).

reports.text: RIGHT DIAGNOSTIC MAMMOGRAM. History: left mastectomy 2014 for breast cancer. Comparison: 2015 outside study. Breast composition: scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No mass, suspicious calcification or architectural distortion in the right breast. Right axilla unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Negative right mammogram. BI-RADS 1. Annual follow-up.

O: Vitals as charted. Heart and lungs normal. No edema.
A/P: HTN controlled on lisinopril/HCTZ - BMP for potassium and kidney function on the diuretic. Lipids done in April, fine. We talked about osteoporosis treatment; she wants to read about it before deciding and will bring it up at her physical. RTC spring.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam, 63. No new complaints. Walking 30 minutes most days, joined a chair yoga class.
PHQ-2 negative. Falls: none. Sleeps well.
Meds unchanged, adherent. Allergies: PCN (anaphylaxis), IV contrast (hives).
Exam: vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Neck without thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Right breast and axilla without mass; left chest wall healed. Abdomen soft. Knees with crepitus, full motion. Skin unremarkable.
Plan: fasting labs today. Mammogram July. Colonoscopy not due until 2025. Bone health: she has decided against a pill for now and prefers weight-bearing exercise and diet; documented that she understands the fracture risk, especially with her sister's history. Revisit yearly. Flu shot in October.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up letter
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,
I saw Ms. Foley for her annual survivorship visit on June 6. She remains without evidence of recurrence by history and examination. Arthralgias on letrozole are mild and she wishes to continue. Given her risk profile we have discussed staying on the aromatase inhibitor beyond five years and she is agreeable. Continue letrozole 2.5 mg daily; we will see her next year.
Medications per our list: letrozole, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, acetaminophen as needed.
With thanks,
Outside oncology group

documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ONCOLOGY GROUP. Visit 06/12/2018.
Four years from diagnosis of left breast IDC, ER-positive, on extended letrozole. Feels well. No bone pain, cough or headaches. Exam without chest wall or nodal findings. Plan: letrozole continues; yearly visits. Please keep the right breast mammogram going.

documents.title: Initial Preventive Physical Examination
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Welcome to Medicare visit, just turned 65.
Functional: independent in all activities, drives, manages her own finances and pills. No falls. Hearing and vision adequate (glasses for reading). Home safety reviewed, grab bars already in the tub.
Mood: PHQ-2 0. Cognition: conversant, sharp, no concerns raised.
Advance directive: has a health care proxy form at home, not yet signed; encouraged her to complete and bring a copy.
Meds and allergies reconciled, unchanged.
Exam: vitals as charted, BMI normal. Heart, lungs, abdomen normal. Right breast without mass.
Screening plan written out for her: mammogram yearly (done July, negative), colonoscopy 2025, PCV13 today and PPSV23 next year, Shingrix at the pharmacy (two doses), flu in October. Bone density - again offered treatment for osteoporosis; still declines medication. CMP and lipids today.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Medicare annual wellness visit, 66.
Health risk assessment reviewed: independent, no falls, no hearing concerns, lives alone and manages well. Mood screen negative.
She mentions being thirsty a lot this summer and getting up at night to pass urine more than she used to; blames the heat and drinking more water. Some tiredness. No dysuria, no weight-loss concern raised by her (weight down a couple of kilos over the year, intentional per her).
Meds: unchanged. Allergies: PCN, contrast.
Exam: thin, well. BP fine. Heart, lungs, abdomen normal.
Plan: CMP, CBC, lipids. Thirst and nocturia - will look at sugar, calcium and kidney numbers today. Proxy form now signed, copy scanned. Flu shot and the second pneumonia vaccine in the fall.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Svetlana - your sugar and kidney tests are normal, so diabetes isn't the reason for the thirst. Your calcium came back high at 10.9. It has been at the upper edge for a few years. I'd like to repeat it next week along with a parathyroid hormone level and a phosphorus. It's a quick lab-only visit, no fasting needed. Keep drinking water in the meantime.

documents.title: RE: Your labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Booked for Monday morning. Is this anything to do with the cancer?

documents.title: RE: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: The most common reason for a mildly high calcium in someone your age is an overactive parathyroid gland, and that's what I'm checking first. I'll let you know as soon as I have the numbers.

documents.title: Lab draw
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Venipuncture right antecubital, one attempt. Calcium, intact PTH, phosphorus sent.

documents.title: Results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with Monday's results: calcium 11.0 with an intact PTH of 96 - PTH should be low when calcium is high, so this is primary hyperparathyroidism. Phosphorus normal. Explained the gland, that it often runs in the background for years, and that her stone history and osteoporosis make it worth a specialist's opinion. The thirst and night urination may well be from the calcium. Referral to endocrinology placed. She asked whether her water pill matters - told her endocrinology will weigh in on the HCTZ. Questions answered.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu (left arm) and PPSV23 (right arm), a year after her PCV13. Feeling okay, no fever. Endocrinology appointment is next week, she says. Observed 15 min.

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY GROUP
Consultation, seen 10/02/2019. Referring: primary care.

Reason: hypercalcemia with elevated PTH; polyuria.

History: 66-year-old woman with recently found primary hyperparathyroidism. For several months she has been drinking water through the whole day and getting up repeatedly overnight to void. She is tired and her muscles feel mildly weak. Background of hypertension, osteoarthritis, osteoporosis, a remote calcium oxalate stone, and left breast cancer in 2014 on letrozole without known recurrence.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg, letrozole 2.5 mg, acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), iodinated contrast (urticaria).
Family: father with gout and recurrent kidney stones; sister with severe osteoporosis; mother breast cancer.

Exam: BP 138/82, pulse 80. Thin, comfortable. Neck without palpable mass. Neurologic examination normal.

Data: sodium 148, calcium 11.4, serum osmolality 305, urine osmolality 120 - dilute urine despite a high-normal serum osmolality. A supervised water deprivation test in our unit produced no meaningful rise in urine osmolality, and desmopressin afterwards did not concentrate the urine either.

Impression:
1. Primary hyperparathyroidism, calcium 11.4.
2. Polyuria and thirst from a renal concentrating defect related to the hypercalcemia (no response to desmopressin, so not a pituitary problem).

Recommendations: drink to thirst and do not restrict fluids. Repeat calcium and PTH with her next labs. We will see her again in about four months.

Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Endocrinology letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The specialist said my kidneys can't hold onto water because of the calcium. That test was a long morning. They didn't say anything about stopping any pills. Should I keep everything the same?

documents.title: RE: Endocrinology letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes - keep your medicines as they are and drink whenever you're thirsty. I have the letter. They'll repeat the calcium and see you again in the new year.

documents.title: Knee pain
documents.author: RN

documents.title: Knee update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know the knee is so much better. They drew fluid out and put a steroid shot in. They called it pseudogout, from calcium crystals. Walking without the cane since Sunday.

documents.title: RE: Knee update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Very glad to hear it. I'll watch for their letter. Call us if it flares again.

results.text: Rhomboid, positively birefringent crystals (calcium pyrophosphate) present

documents.title: Rheumatology consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology practice - office visit 12/06/2019

CC: two days of a hot, painful, swollen left knee.

HPI: No injury. Under endocrine care for hyperparathyroidism. Has had polyuria and constipation for a few months. History of breast cancer (2014) on letrozole.

Meds: letrozole 2.5 daily, lisinopril 20 daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 daily, atorvastatin 20 daily, acetaminophen 650 q6h prn.
Allergies: PCN - anaphylaxis; iodinated contrast - urticaria.

Exam: left knee warm and swollen with an effusion, tender along the joint line, flexion limited by pain. Other joints quiet.

Results: calcium 11.8 (8.5-10.2), phosphorus 2.9, PTH elevated, creatinine 1.2, ESR 30. X-ray of the knee shows chondrocalcinosis.
Arthrocentesis: synovial fluid with rhomboid-shaped, positively birefringent crystals under polarized light.

Assessment: acute pseudogout (CPPD crystal arthritis) of the left knee, in the setting of primary hyperparathyroidism.

Plan: knee aspirated and injected with triamcinolone 40 mg. Rest and ice for 48 hours. Hyperparathyroidism is a known driver of CPPD - continue with endocrinology. Return as needed for flares.

documents.title: Outside letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Rheumatology letter from December reached us today. CPPD with pseudogout of the left knee confirmed by crystals; injected. Calcium 11.8 there, creatinine 1.2. Problem list updated. Will recheck BMP at her February visit.

documents.title: Low back pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About six weeks of aching low back pain, central, worst at night and waking her; not better with acetaminophen or other over-the-counter pain relievers. No fall, lifting or twisting. No leg weakness, numbness, or bladder or bowel change beyond her usual constipation. No fever.
PMH notable for left breast cancer 2014 on letrozole, osteoporosis, hyperparathyroidism.
O: Vitals as charted. Tender to percussion over the lower lumbar spinous processes. Straight-leg raise negative. Strength, reflexes and sensation in the legs normal.
A: Night-predominant back pain in a woman with prior breast cancer - needs evaluation for spread to bone before calling it mechanical; osteoporotic fracture is the other concern.
P: Called her oncologist's office while she was here; they are moving her yearly visit up to early December and will order a bone scan beforehand. Acetaminophen as before. Return precautions for weakness, numbness, or bladder or bowel loss.

reports.text: Whole-body planar bone scintigraphy after IV Tc-99m MDP. Increased radiotracer uptake in multiple lumbar vertebral bodies. Remainder of the skeleton shows physiologic distribution. Kidneys and bladder visualized normally.
reports.conclusion: Multiple foci of increased uptake in the lumbar vertebrae, compatible with osseous metastases in this patient with a history of breast cancer.

documents.title: Oncology visit
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ONCOLOGY GROUP - Clinic note, 12/10/2020

Ms. Foley is a 67-year-old woman treated in 2014 for left breast IDC (mastectomy, sentinel node biopsy, adjuvant chemotherapy) and on letrozole since. Her primary care physician called about two months of lower back pain that is worse at night and has not responded to over-the-counter analgesics. She recalls no injury. She also has hypercalcemia from primary hyperparathyroidism and had pseudogout of the knee last December.

Exam: tenderness over the lumbar vertebrae. Neurologic exam of the lower extremities normal.

Labs: calcium 11.2, albumin 4.0, alkaline phosphatase 120, creatinine 0.9.
Bone scan 12/8: increased uptake in multiple lumbar vertebrae.

Assessment: recurrent breast cancer, now metastatic to bone (stage IV).

Plan:
- Continue letrozole 2.5 mg daily.
- Pain: morphine sulfate extended-release 30 mg every 12 hours and gabapentin 300 mg three times daily; acetaminophen as needed may continue.
- Opioid agreement and bowel precautions reviewed.
- Return in 6 weeks.

Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), iodinated contrast (urticaria).

documents.title: Acute visit - toe
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: right big toe.
HPI: 68-year-old woman with breast cancer metastatic to bone and known CPPD (left knee pseudogout 2019). Woke two nights ago with sudden, severe pain at the base of the right big toe; since then it has become more swollen, red and painful - can't bear the bedsheet on it. Never had anything like it before. No fever or chills. No injury.
Meds reviewed: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, atorvastatin 20, letrozole 2.5, morphine ER 30 q12h, gabapentin 300 TID, acetaminophen prn, PEG daily.
Vitals: T 36.8, BP 130/80, HR 76, RR 16.
Exam: right first MTP joint swollen, red and exquisitely tender to light touch; mild warmth over the dorsum. Ankle and midfoot otherwise normal. Left knee quiet.
Labs: uric acid back this afternoon at 10.2.
Assessment: acute gout of the right first MTP, almost certainly driven by the thiazide (father also had gout). Clinical picture classic for podagra, so no aspiration today.
Plan:
- Colchicine 1.2 mg now and 0.6 mg an hour later, then 0.6 mg twice daily until settled. Avoiding NSAIDs with her kidneys, ACE inhibitor and diuretic.
- Keep HCTZ for now since her BP is well controlled on the pair; revisit if attacks recur.
- Ice, elevate. No urate-lowering therapy after a first attack.
- Call if fever or not improving in 3 days.

documents.title: Toe
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The toe is about 80% better and I can wear a slipper again. Can I stop the colchicine now?

documents.title: RE: Toe
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes - once the pain is gone you can stop the colchicine. Let me know if it comes back.

Plan: gout episode closed out on the problem list. BMP for calcium and kidneys. Continue current meds. Video visit in late summer, wellness in September.

Was in the hospital Monday through yesterday: bad headache on the right side for two weeks, jaw pain when chewing, and Monday morning her right eye went blurry, so she went to the ED. Told it was giant cell arteritis; had IV steroids for three days and a biopsy from her temple. Home on prednisone 60 mg a day. Right eye still blurry. documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen within a week of discharge (admitted 11/28-12/1 at the community teaching hospital; summary not yet received - history from patient and her discharge med sheet).
Story: two weeks of throbbing right temple headache, worse brushing her hair, jaw tiring and aching when chewing, low-grade fevers and fatigue, then blurred vision in the right eye on the morning of 11/28. ED found tender, prominent temporal arteries and a pale, swollen right optic disc; sed rate and CRP high. Three days of IV methylprednisolone, temporal artery biopsy, eye consult. Discharged on prednisone 60 mg.
Today: headache gone, jaw fine. Right-eye vision still blurred, no change since discharge. Sleeping poorly on the prednisone, otherwise okay.
Meds reconciled: prednisone 60 daily added; others unchanged (lisinopril, HCTZ, atorvastatin, letrozole, morphine ER, gabapentin, PEG, acetaminophen prn).
Exam: BP and vitals as charted. Temporal arteries no longer tender. Right visual acuity reduced on near card; formal eye exam deferred to ophthalmology. Heart and lungs normal.
A/P:
1. Giant cell arteritis with right-eye visual loss - continue prednisone 60, do not stop abruptly. Rheumatology referral placed to manage the taper (hospital also asked them). Ophthalmology follow-up through the hospital.
2. Long-term steroids - watch glucose and BP at visits.
3. Requested hospital records.

reports.text: Specimen: right temporal artery, biopsy, 2.1 cm. Microscopic: transmural inflammation with granulomatous infiltrate including multinucleated giant cells, disruption of the internal elastic lamina, and intimal thickening.
reports.conclusion: Right temporal artery: granulomatous (giant cell) arteritis.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
COMMUNITY TEACHING HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 11/28/2022 via the emergency department. Discharged 12/01/2022.

Presentation: 69-year-old woman with stage IV breast cancer to bone, prior hypercalcemia from hyperparathyroidism and prior pseudogout. Two weeks of severe, pulsating right temporal headache aggravated by combing her hair, intermittent jaw claudication with chewing, low-grade fevers and malaise. New blurred vision in the right eye starting the morning of arrival.

ED exam: prominent, tender temporal arteries. Decreased visual acuity on the right. Fundoscopy: pale right optic disc with blurred margins.
Labs: ESR 85 mm/hr, CRP 4.5 mg/dL, hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, platelets 450,000.

Hospital course: methylprednisolone 1 g IV daily for 3 days started in the ED. Ophthalmology consulted and agreed the right optic disc findings fit arteritic involvement. Right temporal artery biopsy on 11/30 showed granulomatous arteritis. Right-eye vision did not improve during the stay.

Discharge diagnosis: giant cell arteritis with right-eye visual loss.

Discharge medications: prednisone 60 mg daily (new). Continue lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg, letrozole 2.5 mg, morphine ER 30 mg q12h, gabapentin 300 mg TID, polyethylene glycol daily, acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Follow-up: rheumatology in 4-6 weeks for steroid taper; ophthalmology in 2 weeks; PCP within 1 week.

documents.title: Discharge summary reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Summary arrived. Biopsy-proven GCA. Matches what she told us; lists already updated on 12/7. Note ESR 85, CRP 4.5 mg/dL, Hgb 11.2, plt 450 at presentation.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology practice. Seen 1/11/2023 after admission for biopsy-proven giant cell arteritis.

She has had no headache or jaw pain since the IV pulse. Scalp no longer tender. Right-eye vision remains reduced and is followed by ophthalmology. Prednisone 60 mg daily since discharge; sleep is broken and appetite up, otherwise tolerating it.

Exam: temporal arteries non-tender. No synovitis.
Labs today: ESR 22, CRP 0.6 mg/dL.

Assessment: GCA, clinically and biochemically quiet on high-dose prednisone.

Plan: taper prednisone by 10 mg every two weeks to 20 mg, then more slowly, aiming to be off in roughly a year if no relapse. Written schedule given. We will check inflammatory markers at each visit. She knows to call at once for any new headache, jaw pain or visual change.

Allergies: penicillin, iodinated contrast.

Video, at home. Following the rheumatology taper; now down to 30 mg a day on their written schedule. No headache or jaw symptoms. Right eye vision unchanged; ophthalmology following. Sleeping better as the dose comes down. Home BP 120s-130s.
Appears well.
Plan: continue the taper per rheumatology. In-person visit with labs in May.

OUTSIDE ONCOLOGY GROUP - note of 11/20/2023, faxed on request.

HR-positive breast cancer metastatic to bone, on letrozole. Rheumatology tapered her GCA prednisone off on 11/1/2023. Since coming off steroids she reports more aching through the lumbar spine, which the prednisone had been masking. No new focal symptoms. Morphine ER 30 mg q12h and gabapentin 300 mg TID continue.

documents.title: ED visit report
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called to tell us she was in the ED Friday. For about a month she had been getting more tired and muddled, constipated, weak and off her food, and last week started vomiting. ED said her calcium was very high from the cancer in her bones. They gave IV fluids and an IV bone-strengthening drug (she thinks zoledronic) and sent her home that night. They did x-rays of her bones, a head CT without dye and an EKG. Feels clearer today, eating a little. Oncology appointment next week. She does not have discharge papers. Requested ED records and imaging. Reviewed with PCP, who added hypercalcemia to her problem list; pt to call if confusion or vomiting returns.

reports.text: Skeletal survey: skull, spine, pelvis, ribs, and long bones. Multiple lytic lesions involving the vertebrae, the pelvis and several ribs. Long bones and skull without lytic lesion. No acute fracture.
reports.conclusion: Multiple lytic osseous lesions of the vertebrae, pelvis and ribs, consistent with metastatic disease.

reports.text: Noncontrast CT of the head. No acute hemorrhage, mass effect, midline shift or territorial infarct. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age. Calvarium intact.
Sinus rhythm. Normal axis. Short QT interval. No acute ST-T changes.
reports.conclusion: Sinus rhythm with shortened QT interval.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Discharged 5/16 after admission 5/11 (ICU first) for severe hypercalcemia from bone metastases - second episode in a month. Discharge summary not yet here; going from patient, her discharge med sheet and the case manager.
Per pt: fluids, a nasal or injected calcitonin, and a denosumab injection; told to stop the water pill for good. Oncology visit next week to talk about changing treatment.
Today: thinking clearly, bowels moving on PEG, still weak on stairs, appetite poor. Weight down to 51 kg.
Exam: thin, tired but oriented x3. Mucous membranes moist. BP as charted. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, non-tender. Strength symmetric, still somewhat weak getting up from the chair.
A/P:
1. Malignancy-associated hypercalcemia - HCTZ off the list. BMP today for calcium and kidney function (creatinine was up in hospital per pt).
2. HTN - lisinopril 20 alone now; recheck BP next visit, home log.
3. Metastatic breast cancer - oncology next week.
4. Weight loss/weakness - recovering from admission; small frequent meals.
Records requested again.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your calcium is back to normal and your kidney number is better than in the hospital, though still a little above where it used to be. Keep drinking fluids. Please send me a few home blood pressure readings next week now that you are off the water pill.

documents.title: RE: Labs

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
COMMUNITY TEACHING HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission 05/11/2024 (ED to medical ICU, transferred to the floor 05/13). Discharge 05/16/2024.

Reason for admission: severe hypercalcemia.

History: 70-year-old woman with stage IV breast cancer with lytic bone metastases, seen in our ED in April for hypercalcemia and treated with fluids and zoledronic acid. One week of progressive weakness, constipation and confusion. Takes hydrochlorothiazide for hypertension.

Exam on arrival: lethargic; oriented to person and place but not time. Abdomen not distended, bowel sounds hypoactive. Generalized weakness in all four limbs.

Labs on arrival: calcium 14.2, creatinine 1.8, sodium 142, potassium 4.0, phosphorus 2.9, albumin 4.0, PTH 10 pg/mL (suppressed).

Assessment: recurrent malignancy-associated hypercalcemia, PTH-independent, with creatinine raised by volume depletion.

Course: aggressive IV normal saline; calcitonin for the first 48 hours; denosumab 120 mg subcutaneously on 5/12 given recurrence within a month of zoledronic acid. Hydrochlorothiazide discontinued permanently. Mental status cleared by day 3. Calcium 10.1 and creatinine 1.3 on the morning of discharge.

Discharge medications: STOP hydrochlorothiazide. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg, letrozole 2.5 mg, dexamethasone 4 mg daily, morphine ER 30 mg q12h, gabapentin 300 mg TID, acetaminophen prn, polyethylene glycol daily.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Follow-up: oncology within 2 weeks to discuss systemic therapy and ongoing bone-targeted treatment; PCP within 1 week.

documents.title: Discharge summary reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Received three weeks after discharge. Admission calcium 14.2 with PTH 10 - suppressed, so this is the cancer, not the parathyroid. Creatinine 1.8 down to 1.3. Denosumab 120 mg given. HCTZ already off our list. Nothing further to change.

documents.title: Fill history review
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Annual Part D medication review from her plan lists capecitabine 500 mg tablets filled 6/11 and 7/2 from an oncology specialty pharmacy. Letrozole last filled in May. Neither change appears in our chart; no oncology note received since January. Asked oncology to fax their recent notes. Will flag for PCP at next visit.

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just so you know - my oncologist had me meet the palliative care team last week to help with the pain and the tiredness. They were very kind. I am on the chemo pills now, two weeks on and one off. See you in September.

documents.title: RE: Update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling me, Svetlana. I'm glad you have them on your side. Bring your pill bottles in September and we'll get our list matched up.

documents.author: PCP

Brought her bottles. Reconciled against her account and the pharmacy fill history (oncology notes still not received):
- Letrozole stopped in June.
- Capecitabine 1500 mg twice daily, 14 days on / 7 off, since June.
- Denosumab injection monthly at the cancer center.
- Dexamethasone 4, morphine ER 30 q12h, gabapentin 300 TID unchanged; palliative care now co-managing pain.
- Lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 20, PEG daily, acetaminophen prn. No HCTZ.
How she is: tired in the chemo weeks, otherwise managing at home. Sister comes twice a week. No confusion since May. Bowels okay.
Exam: thin, weight stable since May. Oriented, conversant. Heart regular, lungs clear. Diffuse mild tenderness lumbar spine and pelvis. No edema.

Plan: flu (high-dose) and updated COVID today. Labs were done last month. Colonoscopy, due by the old schedule next year, not pursued given her stage IV cancer - she agrees.

Interval: oncology and palliative care continuing; capecitabine ongoing, denosumab monthly. Pain steady. Energy low but gets out for short walks with her cane.
Meds per our list, reconciled verbally; no changes she is aware of.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Calcium normal on the denosumab. Hemoglobin still a little low, about where it has been. Alkaline phosphatase (a bone marker) is up, which oncology follows with the bone disease. Kidney function steady. Cholesterol fine.

documents.title: Missed video visit
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Reached pt about Tuesday's missed video visit. Her denosumab appointment at the cancer center ran long and she lost track of the time. Offered to rebook; she would rather wait for the fall visit unless something comes up. Message left for PCP.

documents.title: Call from palliative care physician
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Palliative care physician called about yesterday's visit. Ongoing pain and insomnia; Svetlana told them she wants to 'end it all' and asked about physician-assisted death. On direct questions: a wish to die, no plan, no intent, no firearms in the house. Safety plan made with her and her family present. Mirtazapine 7.5 mg at night started for sleep and mood; psycho-oncology referral sent. They asked me to see her this week. Booked Thursday 10/16 at 2 pm. Letter to follow.

documents.title: Palliative care clinic note
documents.author: palliative care
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PALLIATIVE CARE - Return visit 10/13/2025

72-year-old woman with stage IV invasive ductal carcinoma metastatic to bone, recurrent malignancy-associated hypercalcemia (April and May 2024) and CPPD disease, known to our clinic since August 2024. Accompanied by family.

She has been through more than one line of chemotherapy: capecitabine from June 2024 until progression, and eribulin started last month. Despite her analgesics, pain persists and she sleeps badly. Today she said she wants to just end it all and asked whether we could help her die. She is visibly tired and has lost weight since we last saw her.

Current medications: morphine ER 30 mg q12h, gabapentin 300 mg TID, dexamethasone 4 mg daily, acetaminophen 650 mg q6h prn, eribulin per oncology, denosumab monthly. Cancer center list also shows letrozole, lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and atorvastatin 20 mg.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis), iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Vitals stable. Alert, distressed, tearful at times. Diffuse tenderness over the bones.
Labs: hemoglobin 10.2, calcium 10.5, alkaline phosphatase 240, creatinine 1.1.

Assessment and plan:
1. Suicidal ideation in the setting of advanced cancer, uncontrolled pain and insomnia. Asked directly: a wish to be dead, without a plan or intent; no firearms at home. She agreed to a written safety plan developed with her and her family, including crisis line numbers. Psycho-oncology referral placed. We talked about what she means by help to die and about how much of her suffering we can still treat; she wants to keep talking with us and with her primary care physician.
2. Insomnia and low mood - mirtazapine 7.5 mg at bedtime.
3. Pain - no change to morphine ER or gabapentin today; reassess in two weeks.
4. Calcium 10.5 - oncology aware.
Primary care physician called 10/14.
Return in 2 weeks.

orders.reason: psycho-oncology; passive suicidal ideation with advanced cancer

documents.title: Office visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen at palliative care's request, three days after she told them she wanted to end it all. Palliative letter arrived this morning and was reviewed before the visit.

S: She came alone, by a friend's car. Says the words came out after a run of nights without sleep and a bad pain week. Wishes the illness would be over and that she could choose when; asked me again about assisted dying. No plan, has not thought about how, no stockpiled pills - her sister holds the morning dose box and the morphine count is checked by palliative care. No firearms. Has not acted on any thought before. Reasons to keep going: her sister and her book club. First mirtazapine nights: slept six hours.
Chemo: capecitabine stopped at the end of the summer, eribulin infusions since September. Pain is in the low back and pelvis, 5/10 today.
PHQ-9 14.

O: Vitals as charted, weight 47.5 kg (down from 50 in April). Thin, tired, tearful once, engaged and future-oriented by the end. Oriented, thought process linear, no psychosis. Diffuse bony tenderness. Heart regular, lungs clear.
Palliative labs 10/13: Hgb 10.2, Ca 10.5, alk phos 240, Cr 1.1.

A/P:
1. Suicidal ideation, passive, without plan or intent, in advanced cancer with pain and insomnia. Safety plan reviewed and a copy scanned; crisis numbers confirmed in her phone. Psychiatry (psycho-oncology) referral placed from here as well so it is tracked. Our nurse will call next week. Discussed that I will keep talking about end-of-life choices with her openly and that wanting control is not something to hide from us.
2. Insomnia/low mood - mirtazapine 7.5 at bedtime from palliative care, added to our list.
3. Metastatic breast cancer - capecitabine off the list, eribulin per oncology.
4. Weight loss - mirtazapine may help appetite; small meals.
Return in 3 months, sooner by message or phone any time.

documents.title: Nurse check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Check-in call as planned. Pt says she is sleeping better on the new pill, appetite slightly up. Asked directly about thoughts of ending her life: 'the wish is there some days, but I'm not going to do anything.' No plan. Knows the crisis line and our number. Saw palliative care again yesterday. Flu and COVID shots booked for next Tuesday. Will update PCP.

documents.title: Fall vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Timed for her off-week from eribulin per oncology. High-dose flu and 2025-26 COVID vaccine given. Brief chat: mood 'a little steadier.' No reactions.

documents.title: Psycho-oncology consultation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Cancer center psycho-oncology service - consultation 11/20/2025.
Referred by palliative care and primary care after expressing a wish to end her life in October.
She describes grief over losing her independence, broken sleep that has improved on mirtazapine, and a persistent wish that things would end, without any plan or intent. No history of self-harm. Supports: sister, a close friend, book club.
Mental status: cooperative, mood 'tired', affect constricted but reactive, linear, no psychotic features, insight good.
Plan: supportive psychotherapy every two weeks here, in person or by video. Continue mirtazapine 7.5 mg at bedtime. Safety plan reviewed and unchanged. We will coordinate with palliative care and primary care.

documents.title: Video visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, at home. Seeing the psycho-oncology counselor every other week and finds it helps. Sleep 6-7 hours on mirtazapine. Still has days when she wishes it were over; no plan or intent, no change to the safety plan. Eribulin continues; tired the week after each infusion. Pain managed by palliative care.
PHQ-9 11 (14 in October).
Appears tired but engaged, smiling at points.
Plan: continue current care. Office visit with labs in April. Call any time.

documents.title: Oncology progress note
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside oncology group - visit 2/10/2026, faxed to PCP.
Metastatic breast cancer to bone on eribulin since September 2025, with monthly denosumab. Tolerating treatment with fatigue. Pain managed with palliative care. No hypercalcemia episodes since May 2024.
Plan: continue eribulin and denosumab. Restaging per our schedule. Return in 3 weeks for treatment.
Allergies: penicillin, iodinated contrast.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Doing a bit better in herself. Counseling continues. Sleeping well on mirtazapine. The wish to die comes 'rarely now'; no plan or intent. PHQ-9 8. Eribulin continues with fatigue; pain 3-4 most days. Weight holding.
O: Vitals as charted. Thin, brighter affect than in the fall. Bony tenderness over the low back unchanged. Heart and lungs normal.
A/P:
1. Suicidal ideation - improving; safety plan current, psycho-oncology following.
2. Metastatic breast cancer - oncology/palliative; CMP and CBC today.
3. HTN, lipids - lisinopril and atorvastatin unchanged.
Return late July.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs similar to the fall: calcium normal, hemoglobin mildly low, bone enzyme still raised. Kidney function stable. I've copied oncology.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Could you renew my blood pressure pill and the cholesterol one? The mail-order company says they need a new prescription.

documents.title: RE: Refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Sent lisinopril 20 mg and atorvastatin 20 mg to the mail-order pharmacy, 90 days with refills.

documents.title: Palliative care follow-up
documents.author: palliative care
documents.body:
Outpatient palliative care - follow-up 6/16/2026 (sent to PCP).
Pain fairly controlled on morphine ER 30 mg q12h, gabapentin 300 mg TID, dexamethasone 4 mg daily and acetaminophen as needed. Sleep improved on mirtazapine 7.5 mg. Mood steadier; continues psycho-oncology. Passive wishes to die are infrequent, no plan or intent; safety plan reviewed. Goals of care discussed with her and her sister: home-focused care, continue eribulin while she tolerates it.
No medication changes. Return in 6 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Steady summer. Eribulin continues every three weeks; fatigue the week after. Pain controlled by palliative care's regimen. Sleep good. Counseling every other week. Passive wishes to die 'hardly ever'; no plan or intent. PHQ-9 7. Home BP 120s-130s.
Meds reviewed, unchanged: lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 20, morphine ER 30 q12h, gabapentin 300 TID, dexamethasone 4, mirtazapine 7.5 qhs, PEG daily, acetaminophen prn; eribulin and denosumab at the cancer center.
O: Vitals as charted; weight stable at 47 kg. Thin. Affect warm. Diffuse low back tenderness unchanged. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.
A/P:
1. Suicidal ideation - continues to settle; safety plan in place.
2. Metastatic breast cancer to bone - oncology and palliative care.
3. HTN - controlled on lisinopril.
4. Hyperlipidemia - atorvastatin.
CMP, CBC today. Follow-up booked for September; flu and COVID at that time.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Svetlana, your labs from Friday are much like April's - calcium in range, hemoglobin a little low, kidney function stable. I've sent a copy to oncology. See you in September.

documents.title: RE: Your labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. See you then.

documents.title: Oncology progress note
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside oncology group - treatment visit 8/11/2026.
Continues eribulin for metastatic breast cancer to bone, with monthly denosumab. Fatigue stable, counts adequate for treatment. No hypercalcemia. Pain managed with palliative care.
Plan: continue current treatment; next restaging per schedule.
Allergies: penicillin, iodinated contrast.
